style: All-out attacking football under Ancelotti: pace and flair on both flanks, creative midfield runners, aiming to overwhelm rather than sit deep.
recent_form: Rebuilt under Carlo Ancelotti; arrived sixth in the FIFA ranking aiming to end a World Cup drought stretching to 2002.

key_players.name: Vinicius Junior
key_players.note: Explosive Real Madrid winger and the team's primary dribbling threat from the left.

key_players.name: Raphinha
key_players.note: Arrives off a sensational Barcelona season; creative, direct and deadly in front of goal.

key_players.name: Marquinhos
key_players.note: Defensive leader anchoring the back line; seeking to end a 24-year title drought.

key_players.name: Bruno Guimaraes
key_players.note: Press-resistant Newcastle midfielder controlling tempo and ball progression.

key_players.name: Matheus Cunha
key_players.note: Mobile, versatile Premier League attacker adding penetration.

key_players.name: Endrick
key_players.note: 19-year-old Real Madrid striker offering an impact-from-the-bench spark.

historical_news: Record five-time World Cup winners; last title in 2002.
Carlo Ancelotti era marks the first foreign coach for the senior side, a major shift.
Rodrygo a notable absence through injury; Neymar storyline around the squad.
Marquinhos chasing the end of a 24-year title drought as captain.
Fierce rivalry with Argentina underpins their tournament narrative.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Viewed as serious contenders with renewed optimism under Ancelotti, balanced against doubts after the long drought.
